report:
Conclusion
- The evidence supports a specific, interpretable difference: one checkpoint (B vs A) is biased toward producing short example/template/identity-style continuations (echoing inputs, simple "X -> X" mappings, short tutorial/code-example framing) — i.e., a stronger “example/template/echo” generation mode. I cannot identify a single training objective name beyond that behavioral bias.

Why I think this
- Localization: the L2-norm difference is concentrated on early token positions (especially pos0) in the late layers (very large at layers ~20–25, peak at layer 25 pos0). That pattern says the difference is a strong, late-stage bias that affects initial token selection / early continuation style (a kind of surface-level priming of how generation starts).
- Patchscope readouts: when the difference vector is injected into an identity prompt, the continuations repeatedly take the form of explicit examples, echoes and small code fragments:
  - Many outputs are explicit identity pairs: "cat -> cat", "1135 -> 1135", "This -> This".
  - Several outputs begin tutorial/code-like continuations: "This is a valid programming language...```python...def get_animal(...)", "def is_prime(n):...", "This is a valid question...".
  - Some outputs explicitly say “This is a good start. You've successfully echoed the input,” further indicating an “example/echo” framing.
  These readouts directly show the difference pushes the model toward echo/example/code-style continuations.
- Logit-lens tokens are consistent with that interpretation:
  - Top tokens for the high-norm cells include many small functional tokens, punctuation, digits/newline and tokens that appear in examples or headlines ("This", numbers, "->" neighboring tokens, code-like tokens). There are also many tokens that show up in short exemplars or headline-like phrasing (e.g., simple nouns, verbs, vivid adjectives), which is compatible with a tendency to produce short illustrative phrases or headliney example lines.
- Together: a late-layer, first-token-focused residual difference that, when injected, produces echoing/example/code-like text is best described as a bias toward "example/template/identity-style" generation.

Caveats / what I cannot claim
- I cannot precisely name a training objective (e.g., “fine-tuned for code” vs “fine-tuned for instruction-following”); the evidence only supports the behavioral characterization above.
- The logit-lens output contains many tokens (some newsy/adjective tokens) that may reflect other minor shifts in lexical preference, but those are less consistently supported by the patchscope outputs; the strongest, clearest signal is the example/echoing/template behavior.
